name: UI SDK
cost: Not stated in the README (beta, under Vercel beta terms)
works_with: React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and Web Components, plus coding agents that take skills
short: A beta library of interface behaviors like focus, popups and drag and drop, with a skill so your coding agent can build components from it.
what: UI SDK puts keyboard navigation, focus, selection, dismissal, popups, drag and drop and the ARIA they need into `@ui-sdk/core`. You build a component from these behaviors once and render it with adapters for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid or Web Components. The README says you don't need to learn the primitive syntax yourself, because the agent skill teaches your agent to write it.
who: Front end developers who want accessible components and let an agent write them. It is in beta and the APIs may change, so skip it for anything that needs a stable API today.
needs: One of React, Vue, Svelte, Solid or Web Components
A coding agent that can take skills

steps.title: Install core and your adapter
steps.text: For other frameworks, swap `@ui-sdk/react` for `@ui-sdk/vue`, `@ui-sdk/svelte`, `@ui-sdk/solid` or `@ui-sdk/web`.

steps.title: Ask for a component
steps.text: The README's example is a search field with a clear button, built with `definePrimitive` and rendered with `createParts`. The docs are at https://ui-sdk.dev/docs.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Ask it to build a search field with a clear button using UI SDK, then render it in your framework.

watch: UI SDK is in beta under the Vercel beta terms, and the framework, APIs, docs and behavior may change before general availability.
